title: Solarium — A Quieter Kind of Orbit
description: A self-contained, responsive planetary observatory with an animated Three.js solar-system scene, orbit/zoom camera controls, planet selection and notes, pause/resume, speed adjustment, reset, and a clearly labeled static fallback when WebGL is unavailable.

tests.name: Vite in-memory bundle
tests.command: node --input-type=module -e "import { build } from 'vite'; await build({ root: process.cwd(), configFile: false, logLevel: 'warn', build: { write: false, rollupOptions: { input: process.cwd() + '/index.html' } } });"

tests.name: Scaffold and static API check
tests.command: Python check: exactly one required module script tag; no fetch/XHR/WebSocket, local/session storage, cookies, or parent/top access in main.js

repairsMade: Removed an empty CSS @import before the final bundle check.
Changed generated planet-texture pixel blending to scalar interpolation to avoid repeated per-pixel Three.js color-object allocation.
Added a WebGL context-loss handler that stops animation and switches to the readable fallback.
knownLimitations: Browser runtime and visual QA were not performed; localhost/browser access is unavailable for this run.
The 3D scene requires WebGL. Without it, the 2D orbital diagram is static and motion controls are disabled; planet selection and written notes remain available.
The scene is a viewing model, not a scientific ephemeris: orbital paths and relative sizes are stylized, and motion is accelerated.
